contract_terms.url_source: GET https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/series/<ticker>, fetched live 2026-08-01, one call per series (not assumed from ticker name, per rule_ambiguities item 1)
contract_terms.pdf_read_method: WebFetch on the PDF saved and re-read via the Read tool (page-by-page text), not a summarized quote
contract_terms.dead_heat_clause_verbatim: Tied rankings shall be resolved using the publisher's official tie-breaking methodology; if none exists, all tied entities share the highest rank among them. If multiple candidates are tied for a given rank, then their Contracts will resolve to $1/(the number of candidates tied), rounded down. If a tie results in a ranking being skipped (e.g. two candidates tie for the #1 position, and the next rank listed is for #3), then a market on a given candidate being #2 will resolve to No.
contract_terms.condition_text: The publisher's OWN official tie-breaking methodology is applied first; the $1/n pro-rata split only fires if none exists and a genuine tie survives. This is the same conditional structure CLAUDE.md documents for KXLEADER* (LEAGUELEADER.pdf) — every prior write-up of this ticker family stated the split unconditionally, and this card would repeat that error if left unchecked.

contract_terms.espn_official_tiebreak_status: UNRESOLVED. Could not confirm or rule out an ESPN-published tiebreak methodology for its season fantasy-points leaderboard. Four WebFetch attempts against espn.com/fantasy/football pages and support.espn.com returned 404, 403, or JS-rendered empty content with no leaderboard/methodology text retrievable. Per instructions, this is UNMEASURED, not resolved in the strategy's favor — the clause's live/dormant status is unknown.
contract_terms.strike_structure_finding: Single-rank, #1-ONLY strikes ('Top QB'/'Top RB'/etc. = rank 1 exclusively). Verified via GET /trade-api/v2/markets?series_ticker=KXRANKLISTFFQB and ...FFRB — every sampled market's rules_primary reads "If <Player> is the #1 scoring <POS> on ESPN Fantasy Football PPR <Position> Rankings in the 2026-2027 regular season, then the market resolves to Yes." No cap_strike/floor_strike or range ('top 12') strikes were present in either series sampled. This answers rule_ambiguities item 3: NOT a range/threshold strike.
contract_terms.cadence_finding_critical: Markets are SEASON-LONG, not weekly. GET /trade-api/v2/events?series_ticker=KXRANKLISTFFQB returns exactly two events: KXRANKLISTFFQB-27 ('2026-27 regular season', close_time 2027-02-01T06:00:00Z) and KXRANKLISTFFQB-26FEB ('2025 Season ... through Feb 2026', already past-due today). No weekly event or market ticker was found for any of the six series.
contract_terms.card_thesis_mismatch: The opportunity card's premises ('weekly fantasy-football rank markets', 'a market pricing a rank threshold') are contradicted by the live product on both axes: cadence is full-season, not weekly; strikes are single #1-rank, not a threshold/range. Possible source of the confusion: a genuinely different, unrelated template ('NFLFANTASY', ticker KXNFLFANTASYMOST) also exists in satellites_research/data/templates.json (line ~16711) and was NOT fetched or verified in this review — flagged only as a plausible mix-up, not asserted as fact.
contract_terms.position_accountability_level: $25,000 per strike, per Member (RANKLIST.pdf, verbatim) — answers rule_ambiguities item 4.
contract_terms.local_corroboration: satellites_research/contract_terms/GOLDENGLOBESNOM.txt (cached 2026-07-26 census) is textually identical to the RANKLIST.pdf fetched live today for the FF series, confirming this generic RANKLIST rulebook — not a hand-typed transcription error — genuinely governs both the Golden Globes nomination markets and KXRANKLISTFF*.

settlement_mapping.settler_code_evidence: grep -r RANKLIST src/ returns zero pod or settler files. The generic Settler's pod_ids tuple (per CLAUDE.md's P-014-orphan note) does not include this family; no dedicated settler analogous to src/kalshi_golf_settler.py exists for KXRANKLISTFF*.
settlement_mapping.trade_store_outcome_compatibility: The repo's WIN/LOSS/VOID outcome enum (hard-coded across trade_store, engine, aggregate_risk, capital_allocator per CLAUDE.md) can in principle represent a $1/n scalar payout as WIN or LOSS by sign of realized P&L, matching the golf precedent — but this has never been implemented or tested for this series family.
settlement_mapping.conclusion: The settlement mechanism is understood in the abstract (exchange-wide pattern) but UNVERIFIED for KXRANKLISTFF* specifically — no live/settled instance exists to confirm field behavior on this family, and no code implements the mapping. Unmeasured, not a pass.

api_field_reliability.close_time_check: Live close_time for sampled QB/RB markets = 2027-02-01T06:00:00Z, a specific date plausibly tied to actual end-of-regular-season, not the generic ~2-week-out placeholder CLAUDE.md documents for other series. However per CLAUDE.md's open-market close_time gotcha, close_time is REWRITTEN to the true value only at the moment a market actually closes — these markets are ~6 months from closing, so this field's reliability cannot be independently confirmed until then; treated as unmeasured for now, not assumed reliable.
api_field_reliability.result_and_settlement_value_dollars_fiel: Documented exchange-wide (CLAUDE.md, satellites_research) to carry a genuine scalar partial payout post-settlement, but UNTESTED for this family specifically — see settlement_mapping; no settled instance exists to inspect.
api_field_reliability.event_shell_purge_risk: KXRANKLISTFFQB-26FEB (the one past-dated event) returns zero markets from the LIST endpoint despite the event itself existing, matching the documented Kalshi purge-after-settlement pattern (satellites_research/REPORT_Satellites_2026-07.md, section on GLOBES/AMAS/BILLBOARDAWARDS). This means even once these markets settle, historical field verification via LIST endpoints may become impossible after some retention window — the same caveat as the golf settled-market LIST-nulling gotcha in CLAUDE.md.
api_field_reliability.webfetch_limitation: ESPN's own fantasy pages (espn.com/fantasy/football/*, fantasy.espn.com, support.espn.com) are JS-rendered or blocked; 4 separate WebFetch attempts returned 404, 403, or template-only HTML with no leaderboard/tiebreak text retrievable. The settlement SOURCE's own documentation could not be independently read. This is an evidence gap, not a negative finding, but it blocks confirmation of rule_ambiguities item 2.
api_field_reliability.conclusion: Field behavior is plausible but unconfirmed for this family; no live test against a real settled or near-settled instance was possible. Unmeasured, not a pass.

external_schedule_dependency.reasoning: The card's thesis is a rules-based mispricing argument (dead-heat clause vs. market pricing), not a timing-dependent entry strategy like P-022's golf round-close problem. The determining event (ESPN's fantasy-points ranking) is itself the contract's settlement source, already captured by settlement_sources, not a separate external feed the strategy must resolve. Caveat: if a future spec adds season-end-relative entry/exit timing, an external NFL regular-season-end schedule would become a required dependency at that gate — noted for the next reviewer, not treated as a current blocker since no such spec exists (strategy state is still 'idea').

blocking_issues: Card premise mismatch: the opportunity claims 'weekly fantasy-football rank markets' pricing 'a rank threshold', but live KXRANKLISTFFQB/RB/WR/TE/K/DST markets are SEASON-LONG (2026-27 regular season, close ~2027-02-01) with single #1-rank strikes only — no weekly market or range/threshold strike exists for any of the six series as of 2026-08-01.

Dead-heat clause conditionality unresolved: RANKLIST.pdf's $1/n split fires only if ESPN Fantasy (the Source Agency) has NO official tie-breaking methodology for its season points leaderboard. This could not be confirmed or denied — ESPN's live pages were unreachable via WebFetch. Per CLAUDE.md's identical KXLEADER precedent, treating an unverified conditional split as live overstates the thesis; here it cannot even be classified.

No settled KXRANKLISTFF* market instance exists to inspect (the one past-dated event, KXRANKLISTFFQB-26FEB, returns an empty markets array — event shell only), so the scalar/partial-payout settlement mechanism, while well-established exchange-wide, is unverified for this specific series family.

No settler or settlement-mapping code exists in the repo for this series family (grep for RANKLIST in src/ returns nothing outside the fee fixture); the strategy has no path from Kalshi's result/settlement_value_dollars fields to the trade_store WIN/LOSS/VOID outcome model.

Base-rate plausibility of the triggering event (an exact tie for the #1 full-season PPR points slot, which accrues to hundredths of a point over 17 games) has not been estimated or backtested at all — the closest repo precedent (satellites_research Study A, award 'tie' strikes) found the analogous dead-heat event essentially never occurs at modern base rates and KILLed that strategy on that basis; no equivalent check has been run here.

extra.overall_assessment: Two of four mandatory mappings pass (fee_mapping only, cleanly verified). contract_terms, settlement_mapping, and api_field_reliability all fail or are unmeasured, and the card's own factual premise (weekly cadence, threshold strike) does not match the live product. This is a clean FAIL at the integrity gate, consistent with prior satellites_research findings on the sibling GOLDENGLOBESNOM/RANKLIST template family.
